subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Bees help plants grow seeds and fruit.
answer: Bees help plants grow seeds and fruit.
hint: Ask what the whole passage is mostly about.
passage: Bees visit flowers to drink sweet nectar. As they move from flower to flower, pollen sticks to their legs. The pollen then rubs off on other flowers. This helps new seeds and fruit grow.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Meals are the best part of the day.
A daily routine can help you feel calm and get things done.
answer: A daily routine can help you feel calm and get things done.
hint: Look for the idea that every sentence supports.
passage: Many people keep a daily routine. They wake up at the same time and eat meals at set times. A steady routine can help you feel calm. It also helps you finish tasks without stress.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Footprints on the Moon last a long time because it has no wind.
The Moon is made of rock.
People like to walk on the Moon.
answer: Footprints on the Moon last a long time because it has no wind.
hint: Think about why the prints stay.
passage: The Moon has no air or wind. Because of this, footprints left there stay for a very long time. Nothing blows them away. Some prints may last for millions of years.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Libraries offer many things besides books.
answer: Libraries offer many things besides books.
hint: The passage lists several things. What do they show together?
passage: A library is more than a place for books. You can borrow music, join a club, or use a computer. Many libraries also host story time for young children. There is something for almost everyone.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Sea turtles make long trips to lay eggs where they were born.
answer: Sea turtles make long trips to lay eggs where they were born.
hint: Follow the turtle's trip from start to end.
passage: Sea turtles travel thousands of miles in their lives. They swim from feeding grounds to the beach where they were born. There they lay their eggs in the sand. Then they swim back out to sea.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?
choices: Sleep is important for learning and growing.
answer: Sleep is important for learning and growing.
hint: Which sentence says why sleep matters?
passage: Good sleep helps your body and mind. When you rest, your brain sorts what you learned that day. Your body also grows and mends itself. That is why students need plenty of sleep.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?

answer: Sailors used stars to find their way at sea.
hint: What did sailors do with the stars?
passage: Long ago, sailors used the stars to find their way. They knew certain stars always showed north. By checking the sky each night, they could steer the ship. Clear skies made the trip much easier.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?

answer: Compost turns scraps into soil that helps gardens.
hint: Think about what a compost pile makes.
passage: A compost pile turns scraps into rich soil. Apple cores, leaves, and eggshells slowly break down. Tiny worms and bugs help with the work. Gardeners then spread the soil on their plants.

subject: reading
prompt: Read the passage. What is the main idea?

answer: Volcanoes build mountains as melted rock cools in layers.
hint: The passage explains how something is made.
passage: Volcanoes form when hot melted rock pushes up through the ground. The rock cools and hardens into layers. Over many years, the layers build a tall mountain. This is how many famous peaks were made.

subject: reading

subject: reading
